name: C. Joseph Vijay
role: Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu (since 10 May 2026); president of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK); former film actor
summary: Former Tamil film actor who founded TVK in 2024 and led it to 108 seats in the 2026 Tamil Nadu election. The party calls itself secular and egalitarian, follows Periyar, Kamaraj and Ambedkar, rejects atheism, backs state autonomy and the Tamil-English two-language policy, and opposes NEET. Its manifesto centres on cash transfers, health cover, farm prices and women's safety.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The manifesto promises every family a Rs 25 lakh state health-insurance card covering major treatments, plus a free annual full-body check-up for every resident of Tamil Nadu.

cut-welfare.rationale: The manifesto he leads builds on extensive welfare: monthly cash for women heads of household, ration and pension schemes, and allowances for many worker groups. It proposes expansion, not cuts.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The manifesto promises a drug-free Tamil Nadu: a chief minister-supervised anti-drug force, detention of sellers under the Goondas Act, and anti-drug forums in every school.

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto raises police pay, risk allowances and welfare funding, but also demands apolitical police administration. Authority is not addressed.

decide-locally.rationale: His party and the manifesto press for state autonomy against the Union government: moving education to the State List, ending the Governor's post, opposing One Nation One Election. This is state rather than municipal devolution.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The manifesto commits large funds to Tamil heritage sites, folk arts and Tirukkural; his party condemned Union interference in Tamil culture. The culture is Tamil rather than national in the Indian sense.

limit-growth.rationale: The manifesto sets a goal of a 1.5 trillion dollar state economy by 2036 and promises to grow the economy, alongside a Rs 3,000 crore climate budget. Growth is pursued, not limited.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The manifesto sets aside a Rs 3,000 crore climate budget, a sustainable-energy economy unit under the CM's office, 33 percent forest cover by 2031 and 500 crore a year for air pollution.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The manifesto sets up a Rs 50,000 crore strategic investment body in which the state co-invests directly in semiconductors, electric vehicles, aerospace, AI and advanced manufacturing.

separate-church-state.rationale: TVK describes itself as secular, but the manifesto has the state fund spiritual tourism circuits for several faiths and pilgrimage grants (Haj, Jerusalem), which is not strict separation. The party's secularism is the equal-treatment kind.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The manifesto funds restoration of heritage sites, a Tamil civilisation museum in Madurai and archaeological digs, treating inherited cultural institutions as assets.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He accused the DMK and other rivals of corruption, said they hide behind masks of ideology and loot the state as a family. This is aimed at his opponents rather than all politicians.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The manifesto promises to investigate custodial deaths under the previous government, secure justice for families and take strict action against those responsible.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality is a declared principle of his party; at the 2024 conference TVK adopted a Tirukkural line on equality of all as its guiding principle and his slogan was everything for everyone.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: At the 2024 conference TVK's spokesperson said one-third of Assembly seats would be reserved for women, rising gradually to 50 percent. This is a party spokesperson's account and covers legislative seats only.

single-official-language.rationale: He told the Assembly the two-language formula is sufficient, with Tamil as the state language and English as link language, and opposed imposition of Hindi. The manifesto also backs state languages in high courts.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The manifesto's public monitoring platform would publish accounts, spending and replies to citizens. It does not mention a legal right of access.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No recorded position. His demand for a fair share of central tax revenue is a related issue; he did not say revenue should mostly stay in the region where it is raised.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He has criticised the DMK as a dynastic family and told the Assembly his party aims to benefit every household rather than one dynasty.

online-participation.rationale: The manifesto creates a digital 'Makkal Arangam' where citizens file complaints and petitions, with petitions of 5 lakh signatures debated for a full day in the Assembly.

open-government-data.rationale: The manifesto promises an official online monitoring platform publishing the state's accounts, constituency and district project spending, and public complaints with the government's replies.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: At the 2024 conference he said TVK would adopt Periyar's social justice and rationalism but not his atheism and is not against anyone's belief.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: No recorded position. A reported summary of his party's call to protect state autonomy does not address whether regional powers should be revocable by the national legislature.

farm-price-support.rationale: The manifesto promises a Rs 3,000 per quintal paddy support price and minimum prices for other crops (also fish), crop-loan waivers for small farmers and state procurement.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The manifesto sets up a separate department for women, children and senior citizens under the Chief Minister's direct control, focused on women's safety and welfare.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The manifesto pledges pressure on the Union government to protect the rights, culture and property of Tamils in Sri Lanka and to press for citizenship for Sri Lankan Tamils in Tamil Nadu.

notes: Most positions come from the 2026 manifesto and party declarations, which are collective party documents. NEET, delimitation, caste census, Governor and liquor policy have no statement in the list that matches them closely, so they are left null. 'Proportional representation' in his speeches means caste-proportional representation, not electoral PR. He deferred the party's stance on reservation. Wikipedia lists him alive (born 22 June 1974).
